newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Burns Philp has not seen any takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Burns Philp has not seen any takeover bid.

text.p: Spices and yeast group Burns Philp & Co Ltd said on Friday it did not know of any takeover bid for the group or the identity of the buyer early on Friday of 14 percent of its shares at a 47 cent premium to Burns' previous closing price.
"We don't know of any bid or the identity of the buyer," a Burns Philp spokesman told Reuters.
"There's no information we have we can pass on to the stock exchange," the spokesman said.
Earlier on Friday, broker Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said it had bought 78.16 million Burns Philp shares at A$2.50 a share for a client that was not an international food group.
The price was 47 cents above Burns' A$2.03 closing price on Thursday.
DMG director Robin Yandle confirmed earlier comments to newspapers that the buyer was not an international food group and that he considered Goodman Fielder Ltd an international food group.
There has been some recent speculation that Goodman Fielder was considering a takeover bid for Burns Philp.
He said there had been 40 sellers and one buyer.
He said the client was an overseas-based individual who does not have any food assets at this stage.
This would also exclude Burns Philp's major U.S. competitor McCormick and Co Inc.
